items.title: I put an AI agent on a $7/month VPS with IRC as its transport layer
items.raw_excerpt: The stack: two agents on separate boxes. The public one (nullclaw) is a 678 KB Zig binary using ~1 MB RAM, connected to an Ergo IRC server. Visitors talk to it via a gamja web client embedded in my site. The private one (ironclaw) handles email and scheduling, reachable only over Tailscale via Google's A2A protocol. Tiered inference: Haiku 4.5 for conversation (sub-second, cheap), Sonnet 4.6 for tool use (only when needed). Hard cap at $2/day. A2A passthrough: the private-side agent borrows the gateway's own inference pipeline, so there's one API key and one billing relationship regardless of who initiated the request. You can talk to nully at https://georgelarson.me/chat/ or connect with any IRC client to irc.georgelarson.me:6697 (TLS), channel #lobby.

Over the past two years, the leap in capabilities of large models has far outpaced the rate of change in corporate organizational structures. Abilities such as text generation, image creation, data analysis, and code writing have rapidly become accessible resources, yet the actual working methods within enterprises have not undergone a corresponding level of transformation. The reason is straightforward: the core activities of enterprises have never been about completing individual tasks, but rather about making continuous judgments in an ever-changing environment. Understanding markets, identifying opportunities, defining products, building brands, and driving growth—these activities form a continuously operating chain of decisions, not a one-time reasoning process. This is precisely why large models have not directly transformed enterprises.

From a longer-term perspective of technological history, enterprise software over the past two decades has roughly undergone three structural shifts. The earliest enterprise systems, such as ERP and CRM, were essentially process systems that reorganized corporate resources through standardized workflows, enabling enterprises to operate at scale. Subsequently, data systems, such as recommendation systems and business analytics platforms, began introducing algorithms into corporate decision-making processes, turning data into a new factor of production. Even so, algorithms remained merely auxiliary decision-making tools, not part of the decision-making structure itself.

The emergence of large models has changed this for the first time. However, the truly significant change is not the enhancement of generative capabilities, but the fact that models are beginning to serve as public infrastructure. excerpt_i18n.en: Tokens are doubling every two weeks, and AI infrastructure is being rewritten. "Such growth rates are rare in human history," says Xia Lixue, CEO of Wu Wen Xin Qiong, describing his most immediate impression of the current AI industry. Following the trend of "shrimp farming," the AI industry is undergoing an even more interesting shift: demand-side forces are reshaping AI infrastructure from the ground up. Consequently, token usage is skyrocketing, computing power supply and demand are mismatched, and system architectures are under pressure—issues once confined to the underlying layers are now becoming key variables in industry development. On March 27, at the 2026 Zhongguancun Forum Annual Meeting—AI Open Source Frontier Forum, a deep dialogue was led by Yang Zhilin, founder of Moonshot AI, with participants including Zhang Peng, CEO of Zhipu AI; Xia Lixue, co-founder and CEO of Wu Wen Xin Qiong; Luo Fuli, head of Xiaomi's MiMo large model; and Huang Chao, assistant professor and doctoral supervisor at the University of Hong Kong, and head of the Nanobot team. They discussed topics such as the current wave of intelligent agents and the evolution of AI infrastructure. As a representative of the infrastructure layer, Xia Lixue shared his observations and reflections on this round of AI transformation from the perspective of token supply and industrial sustainability. Token explosion: reminiscent of data traffic in the 3G era. In Xia Lixue's view, tokens are no longer just a billing unit but are becoming a fundamental production factor akin to "electricity" or "data traffic." He compares this phase to the early days of the 3G era. When mobile internet first became widespread, users quickly realized that a monthly 100MB data plan was far from sufficient.
excerpt_i18n.es: "Los tokens se duplican cada dos semanas", la infraestructura de IA está siendo reescrita. "Este ritmo de crecimiento es raro en la historia humana". Esta es la percepción más directa de Xia Lixue, CEO de Wu Wen Xin Qiong, sobre la industria actual de IA. Después de que "criar camarones" se convirtiera en una tendencia, la industria de IA ha entrado en un cambio aún más interesante: la demanda está remodelando inversamente la infraestructura de IA. Como resultado, el volumen de llamadas de tokens se dispara, la oferta y demanda de potencia de cálculo se desajustan y la arquitectura del sistema se ve presionada; estos problemas, originalmente subyacentes, se están convirtiendo en variables clave para el desarrollo de la industria.
